idee_recherchee.texte: The holographic principle proposes that all the information contained in a volume of space can be encoded on its boundary surface, as if our three-dimensional universe were a projection from a two-dimensional surface.

titre: Qui fait fonctionner la simulation ? Des univers simulés par milliards
resume: Per Bostrom, advanced civilizations will simulate entire universes, so we are probably inside one of many simulated realities. We could be a science project of a higher-dimensional species, watched like an ant farm or an alien teenager's Earth Simulator.
texte: So, if we are just packets of data floating inside an ultra-complex system, then the real question is, who or what is behind the keyboard? Nick Bostrom argued that advanced civilizations will inevitably develop the ability to simulate entire universes. If so, it's statistically more likely that we are inside one of those simulations rather than [music] living in the base reality. How many video games exist where NPCs live in a world where they believe it's real? Millions. If future civilizations have the ability to simulate entire [music] histories, planets, and even consciousness, then why would they stop at just one? [music] We could be one of billions of simulated realities, or maybe our universe is just a science project for some higher dimensional species. Maybe they're testing how civilizations develop, or maybe they're just watching us like we watch ants in an ant farm. If that's the case, we might all just be part of some alien teenagers Earth Simulator 3000, the intergalactic equivalent of The Sims.
